scope: Numerical constant-moment-arm two-tendon reference, not verified spatial routing or physical HIL hardware.

calibration.scope: Train-only joint-reference supervision; nominal friction/dynamics, no per-test true parameters.
calibration.noise_calibration: Empirical residual covariance on the same training references; offline joint differentiation is used only for calibration. No test labels or contact labels used.

evaluation.scope: Frozen eight-motor-channel inference; true joints and contact used for scoring only.

observability.scope: Quiet prepared/released state family, fixed known calibration. Cable deformation is prepared consistently with each state; no global observability or sensor uncertainty proof.

gates.note: Pre-learning gates for this constant-arm numerical reference. Contact tracking and perturbed numerics are diagnostic results, not hidden exclusions.

rehoming.procedure: Known-home jig reference at the first acquired encoder frame. The simulation constructs repeatable home; the jig procedure is assumed, not physically implemented. No true test joint or force is used to fit the offset; all later estimates use current/past motor observations.
rehoming.scope: One-time zero recalibration, an additional setup privilege versus the uncertain-zero test. Not online learning or evidence that other mechanical errors can be removed by rehoming.

caveats: Four proposed motors: only two robot actuators; each emulator is a finite-force boundary-position servo.
The SVG centerline does not derive the imposed excursions. Constant-arm fixed tendons are an explicit reference approximation.
Historical single-tendon results are not equal-information benchmarks for this architecture.
Actual contact labels are used for scoring only; some requested contact trajectories never touch the object.
Physics dynamics omit contact. Two measured motor excursions still provide full-rank length updates.
Conditional sensitivity, algebraic invertibility and neural accuracy do not prove global observability.
Noise/calibration priors remain hypothetical. The actuator's inner servo reads true rotor state, following the legacy assumption.
